feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.08 m, 7 sensors at 20 mm, +/-0.06 m span, y = 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints, mass 0.6 kg) scored 67.95, the best so far. It removed line loss on the oval (84.1 mean), but the s-bend and slalom still lose the line once per run, with max_error 0.066 and 0.061 m. Iteration 6 showed the 16 mm footprint did not help, so sensing is not the limit. Iteration 1 changed mass and track together, so it gives no clean evidence for mass alone. The mass test is therefore informative. Depending on the next race: if the s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m and line_loss_events drop toward 0, keep mass 0.4 kg and the 0.08 m track. If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.18 at 0.4 kg, the body has become too responsive, so move mass to about 0.5 kg as the compromise. If max_error stays pinned at 0.061-0.066 m with no change in progress, mass is no longer binding and the next lever is speed. Reducing wheel_radius to 0.025 m would cut top speed, but the 3 s finish limit needs about 1.5 m/s, and no run has yet completed, so reduce it only if the runs are overshooting the line at speed. Otherwise test a larger radius of 0.035 m for more ground speed.
requested_changes: If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.18 with mass 0.4 kg (iteration 7 slalom was 0.161 at 0.6 kg), set mass to 0.5 kg as the compromise, citing the iteration 7 oscillation data.

If max_error stays at 0.061-0.066 m and progress is unchanged on the s-bend and slalom, the yaw response is not the limit. Try wheel_radius 0.035 m for more ground speed, citing iteration 7 where wheel_track changes did not move progress beyond 0.18 on the s-bend. Do not reduce wheel_radius to 0.025 m unless the robot overshoots the line at speed, because lower radius reduces the speed the 3 s finish needs.

Keep the 7-sensor row, y = 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints and the 0.08 m track fixed for this step. Iteration 6 (16 mm footprints) scored lower than iteration 5, and iteration 7 showed track narrowing was the only drivetrain change to produce a clear gain.
